description.narrative:
Drawing from the positive impacts of the hydroponic fodder production technology that was successfully piloted in Bardheera district in south Central, Somalia in 2022-23, Social-Life <(>&<)> Agricultural Development Organization (SADO) are inspired to apply for this technique that is used to grow animal fodder with higher amounts produced than traditional farming, while also using less water and fertilizer. The system uses water 90% more efficiently than traditional methods by recycling the water in a closed system.
It also allows farmers to precisely control nutrient levels in the water to optimize plant growth and save money on fertilizer costs. Due to the high levels of fodder grown with this farming system, families can produce enough fodder for livestock and then sell the excess at local markets, providing an additional stable income source. Hydroponics has reduced water usage, minimized reliance on harmful pesticides and herbicides, and contributed to higher crop yields in a limited space.
Hydroponics technology makes it possible to grow crops with important potential applications for food systems and household livelihoods in Somalia’s often harsh climate. For this reason, hydroponics is one of the areas in focus for SADO, the aim is to equip vulnerable Somali women with innovative techniques and training that will make them more resilient against drought and other shocks. The project will also enhance the nutritional value of the food insecure household diets by promoting the consumption of fresh,locally grown vegetables produced through hydroponicfarming methods.
The proposed innovation of hydroponics will also address the growing need for sustainable agricultural solutions in urban environment and proposes the implementation of hydroponic farming in Kismayo, Somalia. The project will specifically targetwomen headed households who experience recurring food insecurity due to the impacts of climate change and protracted conflict. The hydroponic farming will offer a sustainable and efficient solution to the above challenge by enabling women in Kismayo to grow vegetables using less water and land, and with faster growth rates, making it an effective alternative to traditional crop production practices. The project will strengthen the women’s resilience through improving the household food security and create livelihood opportunities for women, and increased participation of women in decision-making around crises and climate change actions. Hydroponics technology, a soilless farming technique, offers the potential to maximize space utilization, conserve water, and increase crop yields, addressing the challenges of limited arable land and food insecurity in urban areas.

participating-org.narrative: Social Life and Agricultural Development Organization (SADO) is a Somalia based Local Non-Governmental Organization (LNGO) established in 1994 with the aim of spearheading local development initiatives in GEDO region and other parts of South-Central Somalia. SADOis legally registered in Kenya and in Somalia under Somalia Federal Government and in Jubaland State of Somalia. With its headquarters in Mogadishu, Somalia, SADO has base stations in Kismayu, Bardera, Elwak, Garbaharrey, Belt Hawa and Dollow Districts of Somalia. It has operational presence and experience in the greater Horn of Africa. SADO is a firm believer in the fundamental moral principle of humanity; that all human begins are born free and equal in dignity and rights and therefore action should be taken to prevent or alleviate human suffering arising out of disaster or conflict, and that nothing should override this principle. Our activities are grounded on the rights-based approach on the belief that people are entitled to basic conditions of living with dignity and have access to equal opportunity as a basis of fulfilling their human potential. MISSION Our mission is to work with our partners in improving the quality of life of vulnerable communities in Somalia through facilitating humanitarian aid and sustainable development programs. A horn of Africa in which vulnerable communities live in dignity and security. CORE VALUES SADO believes in, and is guided by the following ideals: respect, moral and ethical standards, making sound judgments in our programming and innovations.
